rationale: C22 plausibly supplied a material drafting template. Both letters respond to a steel-industry request for presidential fact-finding intervention by applying the Taft-Hartley emergency threshold, concluding that the circumstances do not justify a statutory board of inquiry, while emphasizing the serious national consequences of interrupted steel production. The child adapts that framework into a recommendation for uninterrupted production and continued voluntary bargaining with mediation available. C21 and C24 contain close parallels concerning continued operations, collective bargaining, mediation, and voluntary settlement, but neither matches the child's steel-specific statutory refusal as directly as C22.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Congress in the Taft-Hartley Act authorized the President, in emergencies affecting the national health or safety, to appoint boards of inquiry for fact finding... I do not believe it would be in the national interest for me to follow your suggestion.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the present situation in the steel industry does not constitute such an immediate peril to the national health or safety as to authorize the appointment of a board of inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947.
shared_material.explanation: Both use the same statutory emergency threshold to explain why a presidential board of inquiry should not be appointed in a steel dispute.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I suggest to both parties to this dispute that they continue to bargain without interruption of production until all of the terms and conditions of a new contract are agreed upon.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: an interruption in steel production would have serious consequences to the whole Nation. It is obviously more sensible to attempt to prevent such an interruption before it starts
shared_material.explanation: The child converts the earlier letter's preventive rationale into an operative request for continued production during bargaining.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the final settlement should be and will be made by the parties themselves... free voluntary collective bargaining is an integral part of the American democratic way of life.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Those recommendations will not, of course, bind either party... This is a proper and accepted method of aiding and maintaining industrial peace, and is in keeping with the American spirit of fair dealing.
shared_material.explanation: Both stress nonbinding governmental assistance and preserve the parties' responsibility for voluntary settlement.
